doc.title: Chuck Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 7, 2023

title: Train wreck gigs and orchestra triplets
summary: Lamb recalls stage derailments and orchestra rehearsals where classical players phrase triplets differently.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Are you paying attention out there all you young aspiring —
This question usually does not work, but do you recall any train wreck type gigs?
Just in general, a gig that was terrible?

Not really man. Not really. You know there’s been some train wrecks on stage on a tune where it derails and sort of like what we were talking about before, the bass player gets lost and you know you’ve got 150 people there. And they probably don’t notice, you know, as you know that reality in the live gig thing. But you know it usually — I don’t know for some reason I’m just thinking of when we do these orchestra gigs with the Brubecks, you know playing with the full orchestra there’ll be like rehearsal the day — dress rehearsal the day of the concert and this stuff is like there’s parts that are just they can’t keep the time like if it’s triplets, the triplet figure, they can’t play them. They play triplets differently. They phrase them different. It’s a train wreck and we’re like crashing and burning. And it’s like okay. And we get to the gig and do it and it’s always been cool.
But those are pre-gig things but you know those are ones where I think oh man this ain’t going to happen.

Orchestra ain’t swinging. It’s an interesting thing man because to classical people what a triplet is, you know, how you swing, how do you swing a triplet, you know the typical eighth note swing but the triplet one is always the one that’s —
